title: #daysofwineandroses #daysofwineandrosesbroadway #daysofwineandrosesmu...
transcript: Last night, I went to see Days of Wine and Roses on Broadway at Studio 54. The show was so good, but also super depressing and potentially triggering due to it being largely about addiction. This vibe is totally not what you'd expect based on the marketing art, but make no mistake, the show is very dark. If watching an hour and 45 minutes of a couple in the 50s in New York succumbing to alcoholism and destroying their lives sounds like a lot to you, you're right, it is. But the performances by Kelli O'Hara and Brian d’Arcy James are so so amazing and so is the score by Adam Guettel — but I kind of imagine that some people might be turned off by the style of the score which is quite complex and heavily integrated into the scenework. You probably aren't really gonna be humming the tunes on your way home. I loved it though and I thought the orchestrations were really great too, very melancholy and almost haunting. Overall the show might not be everyone's cup of tea but I would recommend it if you're prepared for the subject matter. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer clearly recommends the show despite acknowledging its challenging subject matter and potential audience limitations. They praise the performances, score, and orchestrations as 'amazing' and 'really great' while being upfront about content warnings.
